content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes Differentiable Channel Selection (DCS) to select the most important chunks of feature for attention computation. This selection is input dependent and differentiable. The experiments demonstrated that by utilizing the selection feature channels, there is stronger responses (Fig1) over locations with similar semantic contents. And a bunch of computer vision tasks such as Re-ID, detection and classification could benefit from the design.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 
1. this paper is with clear motivation, and experiment process is detailed and seem to be very reproducible. 
2. the figures are very illustration and helpful in understanding the method (except Fig. 4, which might need some de-blur and explanation on notations)

Weakness:
1. the proposed models, have limited improvements in terms of quantitative metrics over three tasks, especially when comparing to recent mobile-friendly transformer designs. 
2. while the paper only focus on the  quantitative metrics comparison, it is not clear how this DCS is comparable to general networks on other dimensions such as training time and compatibilities with quantization, etc. 
3. I find Fig.4 is quite hard to follow. Maybe it needs improvement on figure quality and interpretations on notations/flow?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
There is no problem with clarity: this paper is quite easy to follow despite a little bit of obstructions in Sec 2.2 (maybe compare with bounding box regression in object detection research?)
In terms of experiments and writing, the quality is also quite good. 
For novelty, I believe there are exist some similar work in selecting/ranking the most important channels in CNN, but the differentiable properties seem to be new.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Overall, my biggest concern for this paper is the limited improvements in terms of quantitative metrics on multiple tasks. The results is especially not impressive when comparing with state-of-the-art mobile friendly transformer models (TopFormer, Mobile-Former, etc). 
More importantly, the other aspects of the model is not explored. From the paper, We only have a qualitative impression is that the model is more selective of semantic similar regions of a target patch. But in terms of other benefits or potential risks, such as: is it take longer to train?

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes a novel channel selection module for computing attention maps. The problem with the previous method is that they use the whole channel dimension to compute the attention map, which prohibits the model from computing a discriminant attention map and affects downstream task performance in a negative way. They propose a novel attention module termed Differentiable Channel Selection (DCS). The proposed method learns to select informative channel subsets in the whole channel dimension. By applying the proposed attention module called DCS, the proposed method enhances the baseline CNN network in important vision tasks: image classification, object detection, and person reidentification.

This paper presents a new channel selection module for constructing attention maps. The issue with the prior strategy is that the attention map is computed using the entire channel dimension, which prevents the model from constructing a discriminant attention map and negatively impacts the performance. However, the author's method learns to identify informative channel subsets throughout the whole dimension of the channel. By implementing the suggested attention module, networks improve the performance in several vision tasks, including image classification, object detection, and human reidentification.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
The proposed method is a interesting approach for selecting informative channel subsets. According to the paper, the prior strategy either uses the whole channel (self-attention) or lowers the channel in a static manner (i.e. pooling). However, the authors introduce a novel method known as DCS, which enables the model to discover which subsets of channels are more informative than others. 

Weaknesses
The proposed method has an obscure learning process, where gradients of the location window are backpropagated. In the DCS module, the integer part of the location window (s, l) is updated by the magnitude of the decimal value of the same location window (last paragraph of Section 2.2, Figure 4, Algorithm 1). And the decimal values of the location window are only multiplied by the value located by the integer part of the same window (Formular 3, 4, 5). This learning process lacks an intuitive understanding of why the magnitude of the decimal part of the location window could affect the direction of the integer part of the same location window. The author should provide more intuitive reasons for this learning process.
The proposed method does not show a clear difference from other methods during capturing semantically similar features (Figure 1). They argue that the proposed method could calculate more meaningful affinity between features by saying (in Figure 1. caption): “It can be observed that DCS renders high feature affinity for features which are more semantically similar to the query, while SA often finds irrelevant features with high affinity to the query.” However, there is no significant difference between SA and DCS in the given example images. They should provide more meaningful figures to support their claim.

Gradients of the location window are backpropagated during the learning process. The DCS module updates the integer portion of the location window (s, l) by the magnitude of the location window's decimal value (last paragraph of Section 2.2, Figure 4, Algorithm 1). And the decimal values of the location window are multiplied simply by the integer value found by the same window's integer portion (Formular 3, 4, 5). This learning procedure lacks an intuitive comprehension of why the magnitude of the decimal portion of the location window may influence the direction of the integer portion of the same location window. The author should offer more comprehensible justifications for this learning process.
Paper does not provide a clear advantage over competing methods (Figure 1). They argue that the proposed method could calculate more meaningful affinity between features by stating (in Figure 1. caption). However, there is no discernible difference between SA and DCS. They should offer more explanation to support their assertion.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The clarity and quality of this paper might be enhanced.
The paper provid a unique method for channel selection in calculating attention maps.
The paper should include a more thorough explanation of how to reproduce their experimental results.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The proposed method is a novel approach enabling the model to select informative channel subsets. The proposed method enhances CNN baseline model performance in image classification (Table 3), object detection (Table 2), and person reidentification tasks (Table 1). However, the proposed method has an obscure learning process, where gradients of the location window are backpropagated. Furthermore, there are no comparative studies in terms of performance between the proposed method and similar other approaches (i.e. self-attention, pooling approach) to show their advantages among others.

The proposed method is to select informative channel subsets. Backpropagation of gradients of the location window makes the suggested method's learning procedure unclear. In addition, there are no comparison performance studies between the proposed method and similar other approaches (e.g., self-attention, pooling approach).

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to improve the self-attention mechanism which has been widely used in visual recognition. The vanilla self-attention mostly uses fixed channels to compute the self-attention map, which cannot give the informative channels high confidence. This work takes this into account and propose a Differentiable Channel Selection to search the informative channels using a differentiable searching method. Experiments on person Re-IDentification, object detection, and ImageNet classification show that the proposed approach works well.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengh
- The idea of this paper is interesting. Unlike most previous works that directly use the self-attention layer for spatial encoding, this paper considers the design nature of self-attention and propose to searches for the most informative channels in a differentiable manner, which may generate more sensitive attention maps that benefit the performance.
- Experiments on three tasks show that the proposed approach performs better than the vanilla self-attention.

Weaknesses
- The motivation of this paper is strange. In Sec. 1, after introducing the background of self-attention, the authors directly claim that `We argue that more informative channels should be selected in the attention modules to calculate more meaningful affinities among the features.' It is somewhat weird. I think the authors should make it smoother.
- The title is too big for this paper. Given the title, I was supposed that this paper is designed for improving Transformers but in fact, it only slightly improve the non-local operation, which is not as my expected. It seems that the proposed approach is originally designed for person Re-ID.
- In Sec. 3.3, when conducting experiments on ImageNet, the authors takes MobileNetV2 and FBNet-V2 as baselines. In Sec. 3.2, the authors take ConvNeXt as baseline. In Sec. 1, the authors use other classification models as baselines. Why not make them consistent?
- There are no ablation experiments to analyze the proposed DCS method.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Novelty and originality
- The novelty of this paper is ok. Few works aim to search for informative channels in self-attention.

Quality
- The presentation of this paper should be improved. The title is too broad. I recommend the authors to reorganize the writting.
- More experiments on method analysis should be provided. I think many readers would like to see how the proposed approach works, not just how well it works.
content.summary_of_the_review:
At this moment, I do not think this paper is ready for publication. There is still a large room for this paper to improve. I also recommend the authors to make their tables more elegant. This would definitely make readers read comfortable.

In addition, the authors can rethink whether they need to focus on person Re-ID given the figures where most of the examples are from the person Re-ID datasets.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes Differentiable Channel Selection (DCS) so that the feature affinity in self-attention is computed by a selected subset (as a union of windows learned by differentiable training).  DCS is applied to both fixed neural backbone and differentiable neural architecture search. Extensive experimental results on three compute vision tasks, person Re-IDentification (Re-ID), object detection, and image classification show that DCS improved the performance for a broad range of applications.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
The self-attention module is of broad interest in computer vision and deep learning. The proposed DCS module is an interesting and natural extension to the vanilla self-attention module. The technical contribution of the paper is the formulation of a set of windows whose length and locations are learned by differentiable optimization, and the concatenation of these windows forms the subset of the channels by which the feature affinity is computed. Results on three computer vision tasks are sufficient to evidence DCS. It is particularly interesting that DCS with differentiable neural architecture search usually renders smaller and faster neural networks achieving better or the same performance as the larger model, for example, ConvNeXt-S+DCS has the same mAP on COCO as the much larger model ConvNeXt-B for object detection.

Weakness:
It could add more value to this paper if the following details are discussed: (1) the number of windows M; (2) the discussion of the difference between DCS and channel pruning. I understand that channels are selected in this paper for the improvement of prediction accuracy, but it will be very helpful for the authors to discuss the relation to channel pruning, which is primarily used for model compression.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The wiring is clear, and the quality and novelty of this paper is good. I feel confident to implement the differential searching method for DCS given the description in the paper, but it will be helpful if the authors can provide a link to their implementation in the revised paper.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper presents a novel and interesting extension to self-attention. I encourage the authors to add more technical details, including how to specify the number of windows and the discussion about relation to channel pruning. It is also expected that the authors add the link to the code of DCS.

content.title: Differentiable Channel Selection for Self-Attention
content.TL;DR: We propose Differentiable Channel Selection (DCS) which searches for informative channels so as to compute semantic attention weights in a self-attention module.
content.abstract: Self-attention has been widely used in deep learning, and recent efforts have been devoted to incorporating self-attention modules into convolutional neural networks for computer vision. In this paper, we propose a novel attention module termed Differentiable Channel Selection (DCS). In contrast with conventional self-attention, DCS searches for the locations and key dimension of channels in a continuous space by a novel differentiable searching method. Our DCS module is compatible with either fixed neural network backbone or learnable backbone with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search (DNAS), leading to DCS with Fixed Backbone (DCS-FB) and DCS-DNAS respectively. We apply DCS-FB and DCS-DNAS to three computer vision tasks, person Re-IDentification methods (Re-ID), object detection, and image classification, with state-of-the-art results on standard benchmarks and compact architecture compared to competing methods, revealing the advantage of DCS.
